defects.observed: A stale QFileInfo from a retargeted in-mount alias exposed OUTSIDE_ONLY_NAME.txt after the alias was restored before resolvePath; missing child destinations were accepted through the inside ancestor.
The same stale iterator path/type schedule returned OUTSIDE_ONLY_NAME.txt. grepSearch did not leak bytes because the final same-handle file read rejected the missing inside target.

Swapping the owned attachment directory at iterator start and during a later AttachmentStore root reopen returned OUTSIDE_ONLY_NAME.txt; restoring the root before the final canonical-string check bypassed that check.

before.scope: Copied actual production implementations, actual Qt enumeration and actual fixture filesystem changes. Test-local wrappers control only the boundary timing; no validation results are forged.

implementation.windows: Open a directory with FILE_LIST_DIRECTORY and without FILE_SHARE_DELETE, validate the final handle path against the immutable selected scope, then enumerate FILE_ID_BOTH_DIR_INFO from that same handle. Retain the handle while processing descendants. Only an explicitly selected top-level workspace/apps alias may be followed; child and attachment-root opens use FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT and reject directory reparse points. Child paths come from the validated canonical parent plus native captured names.
implementation.broker: Validate flat captured names and native type attributes directly while the directory remains pinned; never reopen an AttachmentStore path to validate a listing item. Invalid names, directories and reparse points error without a partial listing.
implementation.budgets: Raw lists return at most 4096 entries and 64 Ki characters, depth 8; any bound error returns no partial JSON. Formatted manifests retain 10000-entry and requested-depth limits. Search captures at most 10000 entries, traverses at most depth 64, reads 512 KiB per file /8 MiB aggregate, and reports truncation. Search stops opening descendants after its captured-entry budget is exhausted.

cases: Original raw/glob/att exploit schedules retained; fixed handle boundary also explicitly required to execute
Top-level alias retarget after validated handle path cannot expose outside names or bytes
Attachment directory replacement blocked while its listing handle is pinned
Raw 4097 entries returns error with no partial list; 4096 returns exact full JSON
Deep chain raw read errors; glob/grep report depth truncation while retaining ordinary matches
Recursive raw/glob/grep never descend through child junctions
Existing formatted alias, held worker cancellation, same-ID replacement and protected destroyed-owner regressions remain green
after.attachment_name_rows: Five additional broker rows added by native_core; final integrated execution recorded separately by parent.

limits: Windows MinGW deployment only; non-Windows fallback has no equivalent same-handle enumeration guarantee.
Directory content may change while open; this is a contained namespace capture, not an atomic snapshot of all directory entries.
Explicit root aliases resolve within the selected mount; concurrently replaced child links fail closed.
These deterministic schedules establish tested containment/lifecycle boundaries, not universal filesystem race freedom.
All mutations used owned temporary fixtures; no external paths, live credentials or services were accessed.
